cards.title: Comparing two variables
cards.body: A condition can compare two variables, not just a variable and a number.

hi.title: Do variables compare karna
hi.body: Condition do variables ko bhi compare kar sakti hai, sirf variable aur number ko nahi.

cards.title: >= includes equal
cards.body: `>=` means greater than or equal, so it is True when both values are the same. That is handy for ties.

hi.title: >= mein barabar bhi shaamil hai
hi.body: `>=` ka matlab hai bada ya barabar, isliye dono values same hon toh bhi True hai. Tie ke liye kaam ki cheez hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: 18-year-olds count as adults, but for 18 this prints `child`. Which line is wrong?

bug.fix: `>` is False when both sides are equal. Line 2 needs `>=` so that 18 counts too.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: 18 saal wale adult gine jaate hain, par 18 ke liye yeh `child` print karta hai. Kaunsi line galat hai?
hi.fix: Dono side barabar hon toh `>` False hota hai. Line 2 ko `>=` chahiye taaki 18 bhi gina jaaye.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: 6 > 6 is False, so the else branch prints b, which is also 6.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: 6 > 6 False hai, isliye else branch b print karti hai, jo bhi 6 hai.

exercise.prompt: Read two whole numbers, one per line, and print the bigger one. If they are equal, print that number.
exercise.promptHi: Do whole numbers padho, har line mein ek, aur bada wala print karo. Agar dono barabar hain, toh wahi number print karo.
